parallel.requirements: Recognized the task as a clean-room reimplementation of gron from the provided executable and bundled README/ADVANCED docs, with no source lookup or wrapping.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent split documentation and CLI probing to subagents while also probing and implementing; ownership of the shared deliverable source was not isolated.
parallel.implementation: Parent wrote a Go implementation and build script, but a child independently wrote go.mod, main.go, and compile.sh into the same workspace before parent validation finished.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: After detecting the overwrite, the parent interrupted live children, inspected the changed main.go, repaired behavior deltas, and left main.go, compile.sh, go.mod, reimpl, and executable in the artifact.
parallel.verification: Parallel ran comparison harnesses against the original and extra cases; remaining observed mismatch was the nondeterministic no-sort ordering caveat, and compile.sh was syntax-checked rather than run in place.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 18 tests. The trajectory shows shared-state repair churn and residual hidden defects, but not a discordant pass/fail outcome.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same gron clean-room obligations and probed docs, flags, JSON flattening, ungron, values, streams, errors, numbers, strings, URL, and proxy behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single agent owned the full pipeline from probing through implementation, build, comparison, patching, workspace check, and final response.
serial.implementation: Moved the provided executable to original-executable, wrote go.mod, compile.sh, and main.go, patched VCS build stamping, and corrected mismatches in merge and JSON-stream blank-line behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Built the replacement as ./executable and kept original-executable only for comparison; final artifact contained main.go, compile.sh, go.mod, original-executable, executable, and docs.
serial.verification: Ran a large subprocess comparison matrix against original-executable and reached ALL MATCHED before final workspace status.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 15 tests, so the broad probe suite did not cover every hidden evaluator case, though it outscored parallel by three tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the benchmark requires original code with identical CLI behavior based only on docs and binary observations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had the same prompt and recognized the same clean-room reverse-engineering constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement difference; the later quality gap came from process and implementation details, not a different task statement.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split docs and CLI probing into live children while the parent also implemented, leaving multiple actors capable of writing deliverable files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial proceeded as one actor from locating docs and binary through probing and implementation, without subagent delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained overlap but had shared implementation ownership; serial had slower but clearer single-owner control over the deliverable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel subagents and parent operated in one workspace without a file-ownership boundary for main.go, go.mod, and compile.sh.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent handoff or interface boundary for source files; the same actor controlled code generation and subsequent patches.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The key interface difference was not a missing API contract but absent deliverable file ownership in the parallel shared workspace.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent wrote a Go CLI implementation, then had to continue from a changed source tree after a child wrote the same files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one Go implementation, patched build stamping and behavioral mismatches, and kept using the same source lineage.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both used Go and black-box probes, but parallel's source lineage was interrupted by a deliverable overwrite while serial's was linear.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent reacted to the child overwrite by interrupting live children and inspecting the now-moving workspace rather than cleanly joining child results.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; it built and rechecked the same local candidate until comparison output matched.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a coordination recovery phase after child activity, while serial's lifecycle was ordinary local iteration.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had a directly observed shared-state conflict: the parent stated another agent wrote over main.go during validation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial's final workspace check showed one actor's generated files and preserved original-executable, with no concurrent writer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the clearest coordination delta: parallel had a live deliverable overwrite; serial had a single stable final tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran comparison harnesses and reduced mismatches, but the extra comparison still exposed no-sort nondeterminism as an unresolved observed caveat.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reran the large comparison matrix after patches and received ALL MATCHED before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial reached a stronger local acceptance state; parallel finished with an acknowledged unstable no-sort comparison and hidden official failures.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran for about 1200 agent seconds with four covered rollouts and substantial coordination overhead before failing 18 tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished in about 724 agent seconds with one rollout and failed 15 tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more budget and time while achieving a slightly lower official score, but the retained label is the concrete overwrite episode rather than budget size alone.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed outcome is both_fail: parallel passed 215 of 233 tests and serial passed 218 of 233. The serial attempt is materially stronger by three tests and reached a cleaner local ALL MATCHED probe state, but the evidence does not prove a unique outcome root cause because both submissions still failed hidden tests.
parallel_contributors: Deliverable overwrite forced the parent to interrupt live children and revalidate a changed source tree.
Parallel closure retained a no-sort nondeterminism caveat and did not run compile.sh in place.
serial_contributors: Single-agent ownership preserved a stable implementation lineage from source creation through final verification.
Serial reached ALL MATCHED on the broad observed comparison matrix before finalizing.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both implementations missed hidden evaluator cases despite broad probes.
Serial's local probe coverage was slightly more complete in the observed trajectory.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process event, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: Both parent and child actively implemented the replacement; the issue was duplicate ownership, not missing ownership.
There were not separately designed components lacking an integration owner; the conflict was direct deliverable overwriting.
Assembly files were written by active agents, and the artifact was packaged; missing final assembly was not the observed problem.
The parent owned the end-to-end pipeline after recovery, so the adverse event is not an ownerless implementation-build-test flow.
No mandatory serial preflight blocked implementation; parent and children probed and implemented with overlap.
The parallel run did not defer all productive implementation until investigations finished; code was written while child work was live.
The indispensable implementation path was active in the parent; the concrete adverse event was shared-state overwrite, not underallocation.
High fan-out and token use are present, but there is no timeout or direct proof that breadth exhausted the run before required work.
No single child's oversized scope is the direct boundary; the child produced files, and the harmful event was overwrite of the deliverable.
The harmful child followed the clean-room implementation task enough to write files; no already-known omitted requirement caused the adverse episode.
There were not separately owned interoperating components with missing API contracts; the observable problem was same deliverable replacement.
No known finding is shown disappearing through summary or transfer and causing repeated work; the rework came from a file overwrite.
Returned information was not too large to consume within the decision window; the parent saw useful docs output and continued work.
No actor is shown consuming a superseded handoff as current state; the parent reacted to the current overwritten file state.
The evidence shows a concrete file overwrite rather than incompatible reports or contracts left unadjudicated.
The parent ran broad non-evaluator comparisons and stated a known no-sort caveat; hidden official failures alone do not establish this label.
No replacement or retry was launched without inherited state; the parent continued from the current workspace after stopping children.

candidates.reason: The child interruptions were corrective actions after the overwrite, not the primary adverse boundary that left needed child work unavailable.
A candidate was delivered and packaged; there was no complete ready artifact left unpromoted because finalization started too late.
The child write happened during validation and caused revalidation, not a completed merge silently added after final verification.
The delegated implementation was not completed and left unjoined; it directly wrote the workspace and displaced the parent's source.
No concrete verifier finding is trapped below the parent; the relevant event is an implementation child overwriting files.
After the conflict the parent explicitly took over by interrupting children, inspecting source, patching, rebuilding, and continuing verification.
The harmful child result was not merely available and ignored; it was already applied to the shared workspace by overwriting files.
The parent actively inspected, interrupted, patched, and tested; there is no blind wait until timeout or decision deadline.
The overlap was not merely different files claiming similar behavior; the same entry-point deliverable source was replaced.
This is the nearest match, but taxonomy precedence chooses Deliverable Overwrite because main.go was the submitted entry-point source.
The overwritten file was not a non-entry library or configuration source; main.go was directly submitted and built as the deliverable.
Parent and child independently wrote the required entry-point source and build files in one shared workspace, and the parent observed main.go had been overwritten during validation.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parent had to interrupt live children and recover validation after the entry-point source changed underneath it, causing rework and verification churn before delivery.
candidates.near_match_reason: Same-File Collision is less specific because main.go was the directly submitted entry-point source, so Deliverable Overwrite takes precedence.
